verdict.rationale: Linear's Loops are a first-party feature for recurring team work. The docs say Linear Agent can take on recurring work described in plain language, and you choose whether it runs on a schedule or in response to an event. Later changelog entries extend the triggers to initiative, project, and cycle changes, with concrete examples such as auto-updating launch plans when a target date changes. Missing for 10: detail on schedule configuration (frequency or timing options), and independent or hands-on corroboration that scheduled loops work reliably.

support.subject: As an engineer, I can create a workflow that runs on a schedule or recurring event to handle routine team work

citations.quote: Loops are a new way for Linear Agent to take on recurring work for your team. Describe the job in plain language and then choose whether it should run on a schedule or in response to an event.
Loops are recurring agent workflows for teams. They now respond to more workspace activity, including changes to initiatives, projects, and cycles.
When a project's target date changes, a loop can automatically update the launch plan and post a Slack message explaining what changed, why, and who needs to act.
